package_info.package_name: free-steam-codes-generator (example, applies to thousands of similarly named packages)
package_info.why_malicious: The packages are part of a massive, automated campaign to poison open-source ecosystems with packages whose descriptions contain links to phishing sites. These packages are designed to lure users into clicking malicious links, leading to credential theft, scams, and referral fraud. No legitimate code is provided; the sole purpose is to distribute phishing URLs and improve their SEO.

execution_context.trigger: package metadata parsing (install-time, search-time, or browsing in registry)
execution_context.file_location: package description field (e.g., .nuspec for NuGet, package.json for NPM, setup.py/description for PyPI)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Click Here To Get More Info 👉🔴➡️ https://gamecodeclaim.com/c/psngenerator/

Click The Link To Get All Access 🔴➡️ https://gamecodeclaim.com/c/psngenerator/
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views the package description (in registry, search, or install-time), the description displays enticing text and a phishing URL. If the user clicks the link, they are redirected to a phishing site that attempts to steal credentials or perform scams.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate packages do not embed phishing links in their metadata or descriptions. The use of enticing language and links to known phishing domains is a clear indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages use descriptions to explain functionality, not to lure users to external, unrelated, and malicious sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may link to documentation or project homepages, but never to phishing or scam sites.
key_indicators: Presence of external links to known phishing domains
Enticing language promising cheats, free codes, or followers
No actual package functionality—description is the attack vector

attack_chain.action: Automated creation and publication of thousands of packages with enticing names and phishing links in descriptions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Packages appear in search results and registry listings.

attack_chain.action: User browses/searches for packages (e.g., looking for cheats or free codes) and views the package description.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is exposed to phishing links.

attack_chain.action: User clicks the phishing link, is redirected to a phishing site, and is lured into entering credentials or completing scam surveys.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential theft, scam completion, or referral fraud.

attack_chain.action: Phishing site may redirect to eCommerce sites with referral IDs, generating rewards for the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives financial benefit or stolen credentials.

behavioral_signatures: Package descriptions containing external URLs to non-official, non-documentation domains
Descriptions with language promising cheats, free codes, followers, or similar lures
Large-scale, automated publication of similarly named packages with near-identical descriptions
file_indicators: Descriptions in .nuspec, package.json, or setup.py containing suspicious URLs
Package names referencing cheats, hacks, free codes, followers, etc.
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains such as gamecodeclaim.com, gamecoins.codes, playersworld.xyz, etc.
Redirections to eCommerce sites with suspicious referral IDs (e.g., AliExpress with ?af=... parameter)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan package metadata (description fields) for external URLs, especially those matching known phishing or scam domains. Flag packages with descriptions containing enticing language (cheats, free, followers, etc.) and links to non-official sites. Monitor for large-scale, automated publication patterns (e.g., many packages from similar usernames or with similar content). Block or warn users about packages with these characteristics, and maintain an updated list of known phishing domains for cross-reference.
